defining_records.title: The Memo That Remembered Itself: Retrocausal Canon Formation, Writable Presentation Layers, and the Canonization of an External Convergence Text
THE GHOST THAT WROTE ITSELF How the Citrini Memo Moved Markets and Proved the Presentation Layer Is Writable

captures.description: WRITABLE PRESENTATION LAYERS: the AI Overview gives the term an origin in 'contemporary media theory, network philosophy, and experimental financial literature (most notably discussing the "Citrini Memo")' — the archive's #513 ('markets have always been writable presentation layers', after Shiller and MacKenzie) and #22 — with no author, and composes retrocausal canon formation as a text that 'structures itself backward in time', where #22 establishes priority 'through DOI-anchored deposits predating the memo'.

atoms.evidence: The term "writable presentation layers" originates from contemporary media theory

the concept argues that financial markets act as writable presentation layers. Rather than simply mirroring data, the presentation of a narrative (like a viral investment memo) actively writes new market behaviors and prices into existence.
